A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SkillNav research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original SkillNav navigation results, skill and routing ablations, temporal-subset evaluations, runtime measurements, and a human routing audit.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds RxR-English evaluation, another SkillNav configuration, controlled comparisons, data analyses, and routing failure analysis.

M1.justification: v3 adds an SRDF-based SkillNav variant using InternViT-6B instead of CLIP-B/16. The five-expert architecture, two-stage training structure, Equations 1–6, and prompt procedures remain. Its new switch-only routing statement conflicts with its retained per-step formulation, so that inference-procedure change is not established.

E1.justification: Figure 3 and Appendix K add zero-shot RxR-English evaluation on Val Seen and Val Unseen, extending coverage to substantially longer trajectories and denser instructions requiring fine-grained path following. R2R, GSA-R2R, NavNuances, and the original synthetic skill coverage remain. REVERIE and R4R are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: v3 adds DiscussNav to Table 2, Mixed Skills to NavNuances and GSA-R2R comparisons, GPT-4o to router comparisons, and NavGPT, FlexVLN, and InternVL3.5 to efficiency comparisons. It also adds a human R2R reference. Random is removed from the runtime table but retained in routing ablations.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce zero-shot RxR testing with nDTW, expert-subset and pooled-data controls, and lexical checks sampling 100 instructions per skill. The routing audit changes from 20 cases assessed for accuracy to 17 selected failures assessed using progress before first failure. These rates are not directly comparable. Existing ScaleVLN-variant training budgets remain 50,000 and 30,000 iterations.

E4.justification: Beyond retained ablations, v3 adds skill-set sensitivity, Mixed Skills controls, cross-skill and temporal evaluations, keyword and vocabulary-overlap analyses, expert activation frequencies, and skill transitions. Appendix I provides substantive analysis of 17 failures, replacing v2's brief routing audit with evidence about grounding errors, hallucinations, and controller limitations.

E5.justification: v2's claimed high-confidence 84% lower bound from its 20-case routing audit is removed. The new failure audit reports a 24.5% point estimate without uncertainty. Seed 0 remains specified; no repeated-run uncertainty or formal tests accompany v3's new 'statistically indistinguishable' statements.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive results for RxR, the SRDF-based variant, controls, routing analyses, and latency/token consumption. Default SkillNav's rounded R2R/GSA-R2R scores remain unchanged, while ScaleVLN's R2R Val-Unseen NE changes from 2.34 to 2.39 and OSR from 87 to 88. Newly evaluated GPT-4o leads Table 4 with 58.16% SR and 48.96% SPL on Test-N-Scene.

T1.justification: Appendix I.3 introduces a mathematical definition of routing success as the mean fraction of routing steps preceding the first failure, differing from v2's reported routing accuracy. The navigation formulation and Equations 1–6 remain unchanged; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: atomic skill specialists coordinated by VLM routing, automatically synthesized skill supervision, and competitive R2R performance with state-of-the-art GSA-R2R generalization. New evaluations support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands explanations of semantic skill atomicity, modularity versus data augmentation, visual-grounding failures, R2R performance saturation, and baseline memorization. It replaces v2's synthetic-bias caveat with stronger arguments against leakage, while adding substantive qualifications about taxonomy completeness, continuous-control adaptation, and latency-constrained deployment.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds optimizer, feature dimensions, context length, decoding, vLLM, checkpoint, and routing configuration details. Original training budgets and five prompt listings remain, while v2's project/code URL disappears. Some new disclosures conflict internally, including SRDF versus ScaleVLN augmentation and greedy decoding versus five-beam search.

R1.justification: The Skill-based MoE Systems discussion is replaced by Multi-Agent Collaboration in VLN, shifting positioning toward debate systems and planner-executor hierarchies. Numerous general MoE references disappear, while CLASH, RxR, InternVL, and other relevant works are added. SRDF's preprint-to-publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites related work, method explanations, main results, ablation discussion, and the conclusion. It presents routing as three phases, reorganizes the appendix into sections A–O, moves limitations into the main document, and supplies explicit section references where v2 often had incomplete references.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn; RxR performance and skill-taxonomy graphics are added. Tables gain comparison and delta rows, the original routing ablation is split into two tables, and the temporal-results table is transposed and expanded. Typography and float placement change throughout, while existing qualitative, skill-frequency, and path-length figures are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses v2's limited validation with RxR transfer, mixed-data controls, and detailed failure analysis. However, important additions contain inconsistencies: Table 10 reports SPL 43.02 above SR 36.67; Table 14 is column-normalized while its interpretation uses rows; and Section 4.2 and Appendix F disagree about SRDF augmentation. These issues undermine several added analyses and the new variant's reproducibility, preventing a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
